High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 11830 of 2023
Applicant :- Rajeev

Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Applicant :- Mukesh Kumar
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Sameer Jain,J.
1.
Heard Sri Mukesh Kumar, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Jhamman Ram, learned AGA for the State.

2. The instant bail application has been filed seeking release of the applicant on bail in Case Crime No. 192 of 2021, under Sections 498A, 304B IPC and Section 3/4 D.P. Act, Police Station Jahanganj,
District Farrukhabad during pendency of the trial.

3. FIR of the present case was lodged against applicant and four others and according to the FIR marriage of applicant was performed with the daughter of the informant in April, 2016 and after marriage her daughter was continuously being harassed by the applicant and his family members for want of motorcycle and on 27.08.2021 informant received an information through phone that applicant and his family members committed murder of her daughter.
4. Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that entire allegation made against the applicant is totally false and baseless and applicant neither demanded any dowry nor he ever tortured the daughter of the informant i.e. his wife and as some altercation took place between deceased and her parents, therefore, she committed suicide.

He further submits that even from the post mortem, it Rajeev vs State Of U.P. on 19 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/183838379/
1 appears that she died due to ante mortem hanging and her hyoid bone was found intact, therefore,
post mortem report of the deceased also corroborates the defence version that she committed suicide.

He further submits that applicant is not having any criminal history and in the present matter he is in jail since 30.08.2021 i.e. for last about one and half years, therefore, considering the facts and circumstances of the case, applicant may be enlarged on bail.
5.

Per contra, learned AGA opposed the prayer for bail and submitted that applicant is the husband of the deceased and there is specific allegation of demand of dowry and his wife died under abnormal circumstances within seven years of marriage and vague defence has been taken by the applicant, therefore, considering the provision of Section 113B of Indian Evidence Act applicant should not be released on bail.
6.
I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.

7. Being husband it was responsibility of the applicant to explain the death of his wife, who died within seven years of marriage under abnormal circumstances in her matrimonial home but applicant miserably failed to discharge his burden at this stage and he in paragraph-16 only stated,
"deceased was upset from her paternal home due to some quarrel took place, therefore, she committed suicide".
The defence taken by the applicant in paragraph-16 is not only vague but it cannot be also accepted.

8. Further, from the perusal of the post mortem report, it appears that on the body of deceased ligature mark, two abrasions and abraded contusions were also found and further, admittedly deceased died within seven years of marriage under abnormal circumstances and there was also allegation of demand of dowry.
9. Therefore, from the discussion made above, in my view, applicant is not entitled to be released on bail.
10. Accordingly, the instant bail application is rejected at this stage.

Order Date :- 19.4.2023 AK Pandey  Rajeev vs State Of U.P. on 19 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/183838379/
